title: Implementation Project Senior Specialist
jobDescription: Job Title Implementation Project Senior Specialist About your business area / department Amadeus is one of the top ten travel technology companies in the world. At Amadeus we are passionate about building better technology that makes better journeys by connecting the entire travel ecosystem — airlines, search engines, travel agencies, tour operators and other travel players — with the objective to better run their operations and improve the travel experience. Within the Travel Unit, Travel Distribution Customer Operations (CMO) unites all worldwide activities related to the customer journey, from onboarding new solutions to everyday usage, playing a key role in every step of the customer relationship: from the acquisition of the customer to adoption (Delivery) and then retention (Customer Services). Our Implementation Service (IMP) organization is part of Delivery, and our mission is to enable customer success by delivering optimal and efficient services around our portfolio — helping customers maximize the benefit of our offering and ensuring a highly satisfying operational relationship. Within this organization, you will be part of the Implementation Projects & Performance (IPP) team, which provides Project Managers for IMP complex projects (migration, decommissioning, etc.), coordinates IMP Strategic Streams (performance, automation, AI, etc.) and manages Transversal programs (from outside CMO) for IMP. Summary of the role A leadership role within the implementation project team, guiding strategic projects through the definition and planning phases and then monitoring and controlling them to completion using Project Management methodology. You will be responsible for problem resolution and overall project success. In this role you’ll Build and manage the implementation project core team. Ensure coordinated action between the Amadeus organization, external parties and customer implementation groups. Centralize and follow up technical issues. Refine and finalize the implementation project scope with the Program Manager and Sponsor. Identify all activities necessary to produce all project deliverables. Size the implementation project (implementation and gap activity). Estimate and identify resources with participating line organization units. Build and validate detailed implementation project planning. Consolidate and follow up implementation project planning, resources and issues. Define and follow up implementation reporting (reporting structure and content, etc.). Monitor the project and ensure the quality of project deliverables. Evaluate internal and external project risks and propose mitigation actions. Communicate and report on project resources, progress, risks and costs to the Program Manager and Sponsor. Escalate any issue impacting costs, project delivery timeline or scope to the Program Manager and Sponsor. Support the Program Manager to implement the CR structure for financial purposes. Attend the Customer Project Status meeting and the Project Steering Committee. About the ideal candidate Education: University degree (Computer Sciences, Software Engineering or Business school). Language: good professional spoken and written English required. Travel industry knowledge: strong knowledge of the travel industry (at least 4 years spent working for a travel agency, a tour operator or an airline). Project management experience: 3 to 5 years prior experience as a Project Manager. Project Planning & Execution: ability to develop and manage project plans, coordinate stakeholders and drive risk mitigation. Communication: strong verbal and written communication in English; capable of managing cross-functional teams and interactions with customer representative teams (Account Managers, etc.). Technical Acumen: understanding of software development cycles, product integration and system onboarding. Tools Proficiency: MS Project (or equivalent), Excel, PowerPoint, Copilot (or equivalent GenAI) and collaboration platforms (e.g. ServiceNow, Jira). Documentation: skilled in producing high-quality project documentation (e.g. in Confluence, SharePoint), risk logs and performance reports. Leadership: empowering team members, ensuring role clarity and driving accountability. Adaptability: comfortable navigating internal procedures and implementation workflows; able to work in a multicultural, global environment. Development life cycle: basic understanding of the development life cycle. Nice to have: analytical, financial or technical (development) skills are a plus. title: Platform Engineering Engineer 3
jobDescription: Job Title Platform Engineering Engineer 3 Summary of the role You will design, operate, and improve Azure and on‑premises virtualization platforms that host business‑critical workloads. Your work will focus on governance, automation, reliability, and security across Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS), Platform as a Service (PaaS), and data center virtualization. In this role you’ll / Your main responsibilities Azure governance and operations: Manage Azure Landing Zones across Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS) and Platform as a Service (PaaS); administer Resource Groups (including tagging, lifecycle, and cost governance); configure Virtual Networks (VNets), subnets, firewalls, routing, hybrid connectivity; and apply Role‑Based Access Control (RBAC) with least‑privilege policies. Virtualization platforms at scale: Operate large vSphere 7–8 environments (multiple vCenters, 100+ ESXi hosts on Dell and Nutanix, VMware NSX, ~1000 virtual machines), plus Proxmox Virtual Environment (VE), Azure Local / Azure Stack Hyper‑Converged Infrastructure (HCI), and Red Hat OpenShift Virtualization; provide L3 (Level 3) engineering, capacity/performance monitoring (e.g., Log Insight, vRealize Operations), and security compliance. Automation, GitOps, and monitoring: Use Infrastructure as Code (IaC) and Git‑based workflows for Resource Group and Identity and Access Management (IAM) changes (e.g., RBAC assignments, role definitions, access reviews), maintain audit/compliance updates in repositories, and enhance Azure monitoring and logging. Reliability and migrations: Maintain platform stability through preventative maintenance and observability; support migrations and re‑platforming across VMware, Proxmox, Azure Local / Azure Stack HCI, and OpenShift; optimize performance and resource allocation. Service delivery and design: Handle incidents and service requests; create technical proposals and recommendations; contribute to future platform designs and continuous improvement. About the ideal candidate Required: Practical experience with VMware vSphere 7/8 (including VMware NSX; familiarity with vSAN is a plus), operating at enterprise scale. Hands‑on experience administering Azure governance (Resource Groups, policies, tagging), identity and access (RBAC, service principals), and hybrid networking; able to expand acronyms and concepts for diverse audiences. Applied experience with Proxmox VE (clustering, high availability, Ceph or ZFS), Azure Local / Azure Stack HCI (Arc‑enabled management, governance, hybrid identity), and Red Hat OpenShift (cluster administration, Operator lifecycle, Software‑Defined Networking / Open Virtual Network). Proficiency with Command Line Interface (CLI) and automation tools (e.g., ESXi CLI/PowerCLI, Proxmox shell, oc for OpenShift, Azure PowerShell/CLI); experience with Infrastructure as Code (IaC) and GitOps workflows (forks, pull requests; avoid direct commits to the main branch). Helpful certifications (not required): Microsoft Azure Fundamentals (AZ‑900) or Microsoft Azure Administrator (AZ‑104); VMware VCP; Linux certification; plus solid problem‑solving in diagnostics, troubleshooting, and performance tuning.
